It does not provide the specific survey weight variable names or any replicate-weight scheme (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so the exact weighting implementation cannot be verified from the excerpt. For analysts using the underlying microdata, the appropriate approach is to apply the Survey of Adult Skills complex survey weights when estimating population-representative means, proficiency levels, and regression-based associations, and to use the corresponding variance estimation method for uncertainty intervals.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Survey of Adult Skills 2023 country note for Finland summarizes adult proficiency in three domains—literacy, numeracy, and adaptive problem solving—assessed in 2022-23 among adults aged 16-65. The assessment is administered exclusively on digital tablets and estimates proficiency on 500-point scales, with proficiency levels derived from task success/failure and used to describe what adults can do at each level. Finland’s mean performance is reported as 296 in literacy, 294 in numeracy, and 276 in adaptive problem solving, each above the OECD average, with uncertainty shown via 95% confidence intervals. The note reports distributional benchmarks (e.g., shares at Level 1 or below and at Levels 4–5) and highlights subgroup differences by age, educational attainment, gender, and immigrant background. It also reports associations between numeracy proficiency and employment/labour-force participation and wages, and between proficiency and well-being/civic outcomes, while noting that doorstep-only respondents are excluded from some cross-cycle comparisons.
